To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the spatial proximity of energy production to suburban neighborhoods is creating a new suburban geography of extraction, (2) stakeholders of divergent views are engaging in a discursive struggle over this new suburban geography, and (3) the discursive struggle is carried out through the construction and contestation of policy narratives.

(1) the spatial policy discourse surrounding the development of suburban oil and gas fields is a discursive struggle between competing policy narratives that are rooted in differing conceptions of space; (2) this discursive struggle is further constrained by the existing spatial policy practices of local government; and (3) these constraints limit the deliberative quality of the policy narratives, which, in turn, limit democratic engagement in the debate over suburban drilling.
1) policy narratives are a key component of the social construction of spatiality and 2) spatial policy practices are an important constraint on deliberative democratic discourse.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways that spatial policy discourse is used to construct and maintain social and political power in suburban areas of the American West.

the social construction of the spatial policy problem of oil and gas development in suburban residential areas, and how this process is influenced by the existing spatial policy discourse of the American West.
the ways in which the spatiality of the policy process and policy discourse shape the democratic process.

this study reveals how the social construction of spatial policy narratives in suburban drilling debates reveals the discursive and institutional constraints of democratic deliberative engagement and the role of space in the production of social inequality.

this study reveals the spatially constraining nature of policy making in a suburban context and that the discourse surrounding suburban drilling is characterized by a discursive struggle that pits the spatial against the aspatial.

the spatiality of policy narratives is a critical factor in understanding how the social construction of the spatial policy discourse shapes the social construction of suburban space and the social construction of energy extraction.

spatial policy discourse is not only a reflection of the spatial organization of the world but also a constitutive process of that world.
